query: quadruped navigation legged robot navigation point-goal waypoint obstacle avoidance sim-to-real papers
content:
**Key papers on quadruped (legged) robot navigation focus on point-goal or waypoint-based navigation with obstacle avoidance, trained via reinforcement learning (RL) or diffusion policies in high-fidelity simulators (e.g., Isaac Gym/Sim) and transferred to real hardware.** [[1]](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.08712v1) [[2]](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v270/main/assets/ren25a/ren25a.pdf)

These approaches address the sim-to-real gap through domain randomization, privileged simulation information (e.g., global maps or reachability), and hierarchical policies. Quadrupeds excel here due to their ability to step over obstacles (unlike wheeled robots), but challenges include whole-body dynamics, uneven terrain, and dynamic obstacles. Most works target indoor/outdoor unstructured environments, using RGB-D cameras, LiDAR, or proprioception. Real-world platforms like ANYmal, Unitree Go2/AlienGo, or Galaxea-R1 are common.

### 1. NavDP: Learning Sim-to-Real Navigation Diffusion Policy with Privileged Information Guidance (2025, arXiv:2505.08712)
This end-to-end framework uses a transformer-based diffusion policy for trajectory generation, guided by a critic for safe selection. It supports **point-goal navigation** (relative 2D coordinates) and image-based goals, trained solely in simulation on ~363 km of diverse trajectories across 1,244 scenes. [[1]](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.08712v1)

- **Point-goal/waypoint aspect**: Generates continuous trajectories toward goals; scales to high-speed dynamic obstacle avoidance.
- **Obstacle avoidance**: Implicit via critic function trained on simulation ESDF (Euclidean Signed Distance Field) for safety.
- **Sim-to-real**: Zero-shot transfer to quadruped, wheeled, and humanoid robots in indoor/outdoor settings. Achieves SOTA performance; real-to-sim augmentation (Gaussian Splatting) boosts success rate by ~30% without losing generalization. Efficient simulation data generation (2,500 trajectories/GPU/day).

Ideal for general navigation without explicit maps.

### 2. Skill-Nav: Enhanced Navigation with Versatile Quadrupedal Locomotion via Waypoint Interface (2025, arXiv:2506.21853)
Hierarchical framework combines high-level waypoint guidance (from LLMs or planners) with low-level locomotion policies trained via deep RL in Isaac Gym. Waypoints interface with versatile skills (walking, jumping, climbing, obstacle avoidance). [[3]](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.21853v3)

- **Point-goal/waypoint aspect**: High-level planner outputs waypoints; low-level policy tracks them sequentially for long-distance navigation.
- **Obstacle avoidance & terrain handling**: Locomotion policy handles complex obstacles and terrains; policies trained with domain randomization for generalization.
- **Sim-to-real**: Direct deployment on Unitree AlienGo; noise and randomization during training enable robust transfer. Works in simulation and real-world with diverse terrains.

Great for hierarchical navigation in unstructured settings, where general planners (e.g., A*) provide waypoints.

### 3. TRANS: Terrain-aware Reinforcement Learning for Agile Navigation of Quadruped Robots under Social Interactions (2026, arXiv:2602.12724)
Two-stage DRL: TRANS-Loco (asymmetric actor-critic for terrain traversal without explicit maps) + TRANS-Nav (symmetric AC for social/dynamic obstacle handling via transformed LiDAR). Unified policy integrates locomotion and navigation. [[4]](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.12724v1)

- **Point-goal/waypoint aspect**: Supports navigation under differential-drive kinematics; terrain-aware for uneven paths.
- **Obstacle avoidance**: Reactive to static/dynamic obstacles and humans (social interactions); whole-body constraints enforced.
- **Sim-to-real**: Hardware experiments on quadruped confirm transfer; no full map reliance, robust to sensor noise.

Suitable for socially interactive or dynamic real-world scenarios (e.g., crowded outdoors).

### 4. Rough Terrain Navigation for Legged Robots using Reachability Planning and Template Learning (2021, IROS; arXiv-equivalent ETH paper by Wellhausen & Hutter)
Reachability-based PRM* planner with CNN-predicted foothold scores. Approximates robot as torso + limb reachability volumes; plans in real-time with online mapping. [[5]](https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/server/api/core/bitstreams/b0e56765-ac96-4e87-b84a-e10982c3f863/content)

- **Point-goal/waypoint aspect**: Generates low-cost paths; runs with locomotion/mapping.
- **Obstacle avoidance**: Separate torso (collision-free) and reachability maps; handles gaps, stairs, narrow/cluttered spaces.
- **Sim-to-real**: Full validation on ANYmal hardware; fast updates even in incomplete maps.

Excellent for rough/uneven terrains where standard planners fail. Open-source implementation available.

### 5. Motion Priors Reimagined: Adapting Flat-Terrain Skills for Complex Quadruped Mobility (2025, arXiv:2505.16084)
Hierarchical RL: Low-level policy pre-trained on flat-terrain animal motion priors (DeepMimic-style imitation), then high-level goal-conditioned policy learns residuals for navigation. [[6]](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.16084v1)

- **Point-goal/waypoint aspect**: High-level policy reaches goals while preserving animal-like gaits.
- **Obstacle avoidance & terrain**: Emergent local navigation and obstacle avoidance; adapts flat skills to stairs, blocks, high obstacles.
- **Sim-to-real**: Direct ANYmal-D hardware deployment with noisy observations only; smooth, efficient locomotion.

Reduces reward tuning; strong for perceptive locomotion + navigation in complex terrains.

### Additional Notable Works
- **TOP-Nav** (2025): Integrates terrain/traversability estimation with point-goal navigation and obstacle avoidance in simulation/real (cell-based planning). [[2]](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v270/main/assets/ren25a/ren25a.pdf)
- **NaVILA** (Legged VLA model): Vision-language-action for navigation, waypoint predictors, and obstacle avoidance with reduced sim-to-real gap (RSS 2025). [[7]](https://navila-bot.github.io/static/navila_paper.pdf)
- **IndoorSim-to-OutdoorReal** (Google): Point-goal navigation from indoor sim to outdoor real on quadrupeds, handling uneven terrain/pedestrians. [[8]](https://research.google/blog/indoorsim-to-outdoorreal-learning-to-navigate-outdoors-without-any-outdoor-experience/)

**Common techniques**: Domain randomization + curriculum learning for sim-to-real; proprioceptive/ depth/LiDAR inputs; end-to-end RL or diffusion over modular planners. Success rates often >90% in sim/hardware on novel scenes. Limitations: Dynamic obstacles, extreme terrain, or long-distance planning still challenging—future work emphasizes VLA/LLM integration and real-to-sim reconstruction.

These papers (primarily from arXiv, IROS, RSS) represent the current state (up to mid-2026). For implementation details, check the linked PDFs or project pages (e.g., ANYmal Research). If you need code repos, specific hardware details, or deeper dives into one paper, let me know!

sources.description:
Our proposed system enables efficient navigation through indoor environments by selecting appropriate footholds to avoid obstacles, rather than requiring detours. To evaluate its performance, we use point-goal navigation, which involves navigating towards a specific goal location while avoiding obstacles . We incorporate a variety of small indoor obstacles into the scenes using existing navigation datasets  to simulate challenging realistic navigation conditions.

extra_sources.title: NavDP: Learning Sim-to-Real Navigation Diffusion Policy with Privileged Information Guidance
extra_sources.description:
For Q5, we evaluate the performance of a planning-based method - EgoPlanner  in the simulation point-goal navigation benchmark. We found it performs well on the wheeled robots, but can be easily stuck on the qrudruped robots. The reasons can be divided into two folds: The quadruped robot is driven by a locomotion policy trained with RL, the response of trajectory-following often delays and cause compounding erros. The camera of the Go2 robot often heads down and captures a restricted view for map updates, this influences the quality of planning trajectory. Further, our end-to-end policy can achieve real-time inference (>>>10Hz) with a GeForce RTX 5080 laptop, which enables fast collision avoidance in dynamic scenarios (shown in the accompanying video). The robot can operate at a maximum [...] Our simulation navigation data generation approach achieves about 2,500 trajectories/GPU per day, 20×\times× more efficient than real-world data collection, and results in a large-scale navigation dataset with 363.2km trajectories over 1244 scenes.
Trained with this dataset, NavDP achieves zero-shot generalization capability on quadruped, wheeled, and humanoid robots in diverse indoor and outdoor environments and outperforms previous methods consistently in variant scenarios.
In addition, given the observed sim-to-real gap in visual observations, we leverage the latest Gaussian Splatting approaches  to achieve the real-to-sim reconstruction and provide a more photorealistic environment for training and evaluation.
